NUTRITION PLAN
  NUTRITION GOALS
    - Glycemic control: target postprandial glucose stability, and HbA1c maintenance or improvement
    - Support training adaptation and recovery withadequate calories, especially around workouts
    - Insulin sensitivity support through balanced macronutrients and fiber-rich foods
  DAILY MACRO TARGETS (adjustable by client weight_changes and tolerances)
    - Estimated daily calories: aiming for gentle energy balance (about 10-15% deficit if overweight) or maintenance; adjust by 100-200 kcal if weight drifts >0.5 kg/week
    - Carbohydrates: 40–45% of total calories, prioritizing low glycemic index sources around workouts
    - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight per day
    - Fat: 30–35% of total calories
  MEAL TIMING
    - Protein distributed across 3–4 meals with 20–40 g protein per meal
    - Pre-workout meal 60–90 minutes before training: moderate carbs, moderate protein, low fat
    - Post-workout meal within 2 hours: protein 25–40 g + carbs 40–60 g
  FOOD PRINCIPLES
    - Favor high-fiber carbohydrates: whole grains, legumes, vegetables, fruits (in moderation)
    - Choose low glycemic index carbs most of the time; include rapid carbs around workouts as needed
    - Include lean protein at each meal: poultry, fish, eggs, dairy, legumes, tofu
    - Healthy fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds
    - Limit refined sugars and ultra-processed foods; minimize liquid calories with added sugars
    - Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg body weight daily; consider electrolytes if training >60 minutes or in heat
  SUGGESTED DAILY MEAL PATTERN (example)
    - Breakfast: high-protein option (e.g., Greek yogurt with berries and chia) + whole grain toast
    - Lunch: lean protein, high-fiber carb (brown rice/quinoa), vegetables
    - Snack: fruit + nuts or hummus + vegetables
    - Dinner: protein source + vegetables + a portion of whole grains or starchy veg
  GLYCAEMIC CONTROL STRATEGIES
    - Consistent meal timing; avoid very long fasts and erratic snacking
    - Pair carbohydrates with protein and/or fat to blunt glucose spikes
    - Monitor portion sizes of high-GI foods; prefer mixed meals
    - Consider fiber targets: 25–38 g/day
  SUPPLEMENT NOTES
    - Vitamin D and omega-3 supplements as per clinician guidance if needed
    - Magnesium optional if deficiency suspected
  MONITORING AND ADJUSTMENTS
    - Track body weight weekly; adjust calories by ±100–200 kcal if weight changes >0.5 kg/week
    - Periodic HbA1c checks as advised by clinician; aim for stable or improved levels
    - If adverse symptoms occur (dizziness, excessive fatigue, or poor recovery), reduce training load or re-evaluate nutrition
  IMPLEMENTATION
    - Integrate nutrition plan with Phase 1 nutrition principles in the first 4 weeks
    - Reassess macro targets at Phase 2 transition (Week 5) based on progress and tolerability
